title: Gaussian Mixture Models
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose and boundaries of gaussian mixture models.

content.intro: This lesson covers Gaussian Mixture Models in the Unsupervised Learning and Anomaly Detection module. It preserves the source syllabus topic and subtopics, then adds an original explanation, a runnable reference example, and a practice task.
content.why_it_matters: Unsupervised methods find structure without using a provided target label. Scaling and distance geometry matter; evaluate cluster quality and stability instead of assuming labels are objectively correct.

content_blocks.title: Practice reasoning
content_blocks.text: The example groups nearby one-dimensional points into two clusters. Cluster labels are arbitrary identifiers, not ordered classes. For gaussian mixture models, keep the problem definition, data selection, estimator configuration, and evaluation criterion explicit. When results are uncertain, compare a baseline and inspect examples rather than treating one metric as a complete explanation.

content_blocks.code:
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
X = [[0.0], [0.2], [0.1], [8.0], [8.2], [8.1]]
model = KMeans(n_clusters=2, n_init=10, random_state=4).fit(X)
print(len(model.cluster_centers_))
